claims: TRELLIS.2 needs an NVIDIA GPU with at least 24 GB of memory, so it cannot run locally on an Apple M5 Mac.
TRELLIS.2 code and model weights are MIT licensed.
TRELLIS.2 ships full training code for fine-tuning on custom datasets.
TRELLIS.2 includes a texturing pipeline that paints PBR textures onto a given mesh from a reference image.
Hunyuan3D 2.1 texture generation needs 21 GB of VRAM.
The Hunyuan3D 2.1 license does not apply in the European Union, United Kingdom and South Korea.
The Hunyuan3D 2.1 license forbids using its outputs to improve any other AI model.
fal trellis-2-lora-trainer accepts a zip of .glb assets and returns downloadable .safetensors LoRA adapters for sparse structure, geometry and texture.
fal trellis-2-lora inference requires an input image and costs $0.25 at 512 resolution.
fal trellis-2-lora can export a GLB with as few as 5000 vertices.
Training all three TRELLIS.2 LoRAs for 2000 steps each at rank 32 and resolution 512 on 600 cars costs about $90 on fal.
GET3D is distributed under the Nvidia Source Code License and was developed on V100/A100 GPUs.
xatlas has no macOS arm64 wheel for Python 3.14.

Source: https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/trellis-2-lora-trainer (fetched 2026-10-11)
Each request is billed a one-time dataset-preparation charge of $0.10023 per input object (10-object minimum, waived when you reuse a prepared dataset) plus a per-denoiser training charge of $8.34 / $3.25 / $3.38 per 1,000 steps for sparse_structure / geometry / texture, scaled by your rank (×0.5 / ×1 / ×2 for 16 / 32 / 64) and resolution (×1 / ×2 for 512 / 1024).
Supported file types: .glb .gltf .obj .fbx .stl .ply .blend
This endpoint does not expose captions, prompts, or trigger phrases; training is based on the 3D assets and the image-condition views generated during preprocessing.
The archive download limit is 8192 MB, and the extracted dataset is capped at 8 GB.
lora_file: Trained .safetensors LoRA adapter for this stage.
For texture LoRAs, include assets with useful material and texture information. Geometry-only files with little appearance data will not teach strong texture behavior.
If outputs copy the training set too aggressively, try fewer training steps, a lower rank, or a more varied dataset.
Source: https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/trellis-2-lora (fetched 2026-10-11)
Your request will cost 0.25 $ for 512p resolution, and 0.3 $ for 1024p resolution.
image_url (required) URL of the input image to convert to a 3D model.
decimation_target Default:500000 Range:5000 to 2000000 Target vertex count for the exported GLB.
texture_size Default:2048 Allowed values:1024, 2048, 4096
seed: Random seed for reproducible generation.
Only the stages you provide are customized.


Source: https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2 (fetched 2026-10-11)
TRELLIS.2 is a state-of-the-art large 3D generative model (4B parameters) designed for high-fidelity image-to-3D generation. It leverages a novel "field-free" sparse voxel structure termed O-Voxel to reconstruct and generate arbitrary 3D assets with complex topologies, sharp features, and full PBR materials.
Hardware: An NVIDIA GPU with at least 24GB of memory is necessary. The code has been verified on NVIDIA A100 and H100 GPUs.
(Single CPU): Textured Mesh → O-Voxel < 10s
TRELLIS.2-4B | 4 Billion | 512³ - 1536³
Please refer to the example_texturing.py for an example of how to generate PBR textures for a given 3D shape.
We provide the full training codebase, enabling users to train TRELLIS.2 from scratch or fine-tune it on custom datasets.
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2/blob/main/LICENSE: MIT License Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
Source: https://huggingface.co/microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B: This model is released under the MIT License.
Source: https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2/blob/main/example_texturing.py: pipeline = Trellis2TexturingPipeline.from_pretrained("microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B", config_file="texturing_pipeline.json"); pipeline.cuda(); mesh = trimesh.load(...); image = Image.open(...); output = pipeline.run(mesh, image)

We recommend Linux for performance and compatibility reasons. We have done all testing and development using V100 or A100 GPUs. CUDA toolkit 11.1 or later. This work is made available under the Nvidia Source Code License.
Source: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/FlexiCubes search excerpt / supplementary PDF: Marching Cubes performs well when features are axis-aligned, but show stair step artifacts in the other poses. FlexiCubes has more uniform triangles.
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture: POST https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/retexture with model_url, text_style_prompt or image_style_url, enable_original_uv, enable_pbr; consumed_credits 10.

Source: PyPI JSON (2026-10-11): torch, numpy, scikit-image, open3d, pymeshlab (GPL3), manifold3d, fast-simplification have macOS arm64 wheels for CPython 3.14; xatlas (MIT), PyMCubes, point-cloud-utils have macOS arm64 wheels only up to 3.12/3.13; trimesh and pygltflib are pure-Python sdists.
